answer: Agents could earn identity weight only by completing randomized tasks whose results are checked against later tasks, with rewards locked until a challenge window closes. A new identity starts with little influence, so splitting into many accounts does not multiply voting power. To fake a crowd, an attacker must fund each account’s stake and sustain distinct, consistent work; copied answers risk correlated failures and forfeited deposits. Even a sonnet about a walnut in a meadow must survive independent checks before its author gains weight.
